approachQuestion.prompt:
Logs Containing All Three Markers

A log string contains only letters x, y, and z. Count non-empty contiguous substrings containing at least one of each of the three markers. Count different index ranges separately.

Limits and assumptions:
• 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; log consists only of x, y, z.
• The answer fits in signed 64-bit integers. Input is unchanged; return a count.

Examples:
1. log = "xyzx" → 3: "xyz", "xyzx", and "yzx".
2. log = "xxxx" → 0.

Choose one approach.
constraints: 0 ≤ n ≤ 200000; log consists only of x, y, z.
The answer fits in signed 64-bit integers. Input is unchanged; return a count.

options.text: Track the latest index of each of x, y, and z, initialized to -1. After each new endpoint add one plus the smallest of these three latest indices to the count.
options.feedback: A start at or before the earliest of the three latest occurrences includes all markers; any later start omits at least one. An unseen marker contributes zero.

options.text: Keep a 3-slot frequency window. After extending right, remove from the left while all three markers remain present. Add left to the total for this endpoint.
options.feedback: Each removed start was covering, and all earlier starts also cover. After shrinking, exactly starts 0 through left-1 qualify, so the contribution is left.

options.text: Enumerate starts and ends, maintain three counts as each end extends, and count ranges once every marker is present.
options.feedback: This tests every range correctly but revisits overlapping ranges instead of aggregating all valid starts at one endpoint.

options.text: Add one for every endpoint whose prefix contains all three markers.
options.feedback: For "xxyz", only the final endpoint qualifies, but both ranges [0,3] and [1,3] contain all three markers.

feedback.reason: For the current endpoint, a start must precede all three latest marker positions.
details: Maintain latestX, latestY, and latestZ, each initially -1. Update the incoming marker at each right endpoint and add min(latestX,latestY,latestZ)+1 to the total. Keep only these three indices and a count.

complexityQuestion.prompt: Analyze only “Aggregate starts from latest markers” as specified in the method reveal. Choose the tightest worst-case running-time and auxiliary-space pair.
constraints: Use unit-cost random access and arithmetic on machine words large enough for every index and sum.
Input is read-only and excluded from auxiliary space. The scalar or index-pair output is excluded; no candidate segment is copied.
The implementation is iterative with a constant call stack. No hashing is used; fixed alphabet arrays, when present, are direct indexed.

options.text: O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space

feedback.reason: Three latest positions determine each endpoint's contribution in constant work.
details: For any fixed endpoint, a substring includes each marker precisely when its start is no greater than every marker latest index. That gives min(latest)+1 starts, with zero when any marker is unseen. Each endpoint uses constant work and fixed state.
“O(n²) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: The three latest marker positions count every valid start at once, without enumerating substrings.
“O(n log n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: No ordering structure is needed for three scalar positions; taking their minimum is constant work.
“O(n) time, O(n) auxiliary space”: Only latestX, latestY, latestZ and a count are stored, independent of log length.
